- When sentiment is low (≤0.18) and forecast shows a sharp upward move, reduce the forecast peak to avoid overreaction.  
- If sentiment is high (≥0.53) and forecast is below recent highs, increase forecast slightly to capture bullish momentum.  
- Avoid forecasting sharp downward moves when sentiment is neutral or slightly positive — true outcomes often show mean reversion or slight uptick.  
- Overshoots after spikes (especially in 30d horizon) are common — cap forecast peaks at 1.5–2x recent 7-day high to prevent overcorrection.  
- If last 3–5 days show strong downward trend, forecast should not be overly optimistic — even if sentiment is positive, avoid “rebound” overestimation.  
- When sentiment is flat or negative, forecast should align with recent 10-day average, not chase short-term volatility.  
- For 30d horizon, if true outcome deviates >1.5σ from 30d mean, adjust forecast to reflect mean reversion bias — especially if sentiment is weak.
